title: 6 Best Small Generators for Home (2026): Quiet Inverter Picks
metaDescription: The Honda EU2200i is the best small generator for home outages; 6 picks, and 2,500 to 4,000 running watts covers a fridge, freezer, lights and furnace blower.
h1: The 6 Best Small Generators for Home in 2026
intro:
The Honda EU2200i is the best small generator for most homes, and 2,500 to 4,000 running watts of quiet inverter power covers a fridge, freezer, lights and gas furnace blower. A 240-volt well pump, electric heat, central air or a fast-growing load list changes that answer. Below: six picks, what each will run, safe hookup, fuel and carbon monoxide rules.

A small generator suits far more homes than the big machines on store floors would suggest. When the outage list is a refrigerator, a freezer, lights, the internet and a gas furnace blower, 2,000 to 4,500 watts of quiet inverter power handles it on a fraction of the fuel a 9,000-watt unit burns.
quickAnswer: the Honda EU2200i Super Quiet Inverter is our #1 pick (top small generator). The small generator to own if you want one that starts every time for a decade.
picksHeading: The 6 Best Small Generators for Home in 2026, Ranked

picks.body: Rival makers still benchmark their small inverters against the EU2200i. Honda's rating is 1,800 running and 2,200 starting watts, enough for a refrigerator with lights, a modem, a TV and phone chargers, or for a gas furnace blower and a few lights. On its 0.95-gallon tank, Honda lists about 3.2 hours at full rated load and roughly 8.1 hours at a quarter load. The inverter output is clean enough for computers and furnace control boards, and Eco Throttle lowers engine speed as demand falls, which explains both the low noise and the modest fuel use. If carbon monoxide collects around the unit, the CO-MINDER system stops the engine. Owners consistently call it easy to start and simple to service, and Honda dealers are easy to find almost anywhere. Rivals post near-identical numbers for less money; the premium pays for the engine and the support network. At the time of writing it sells for roughly $1,100 to $1,300.

picks.body: For well under the Honda's price, Champion's ultralight 2500-watt inverter covers most of the same ground. Its rating of 1,850 running and 2,500 starting watts gives it slightly more surge headroom than the EU2200i for refrigerator and small pump starts. At around 39 pounds, it is the easiest unit on this list to carry up basement steps or lift into a truck bed. Champion lists up to roughly 8 hours at a quarter load on its small tank, which is enough to keep a refrigerator going overnight as long as little else is plugged in. The CO Shield system cuts the engine when carbon monoxide builds up nearby, and a second Champion inverter can be paralleled with it for more output. Owners commonly describe it as easy to start and pleasantly quiet, with the standard small-engine caveat that monthly runs and stabilized fuel keep it that way. At the time of writing it sells for roughly $500 to $700.

picks.body: The GP3500iO sits between the suitcase inverters and full-size portables. Generac rates it at 3,000 running and 3,500 starting watts, and its PowerRUSH feature is built to help start motor loads, such as a sump pump or a window air conditioner, that a 2,200-watt unit can struggle with. That makes it a reasonable small-house choice for a refrigerator, freezer, sump pump and lights together, provided the start-ups are staggered. Because it is an inverter, the output is clean for electronics, and it throttles down at light loads to save fuel. The open frame keeps the price and weight below an enclosed design, but it also lets more engine noise escape, so it is a poor fit for a narrow side yard beside a neighbor's bedroom. COsense shuts the engine down if carbon monoxide accumulates. At the time of writing it sells for roughly $650 to $900.

picks.body: When you want inverter quiet and fuel economy but need more than 2,200 watts, the iGen4500 is the tidiest solution. Westinghouse rates it at 3,700 running and 4,500 starting watts, enough for a refrigerator, freezer, sump pump, gas furnace blower, lights and electronics at once if the start-ups are staggered sensibly. The 3.4-gallon tank and throttle-down operation stretch light-load run times far enough that an overnight run is realistic. Electric start with a remote key fob is a genuine comfort in bad weather, and the onboard display shows output, fuel level and estimated time remaining. At close to 100 pounds it is not light, so it moves on its wheels and telescoping handle. Its panel is 120V only, which rules out a 240V well pump. For a house with gas heat and a basement, this is about as large as a small generator ever needs to be. At the time of writing it sells for roughly $1,000 to $1,300.

picks.body: A battery station earns a place here because plenty of people shopping for a small generator really want small, quiet power, and a battery is the only option that can sit inside the house. EcoFlow rates the DELTA 2 at 1,024 watt-hours of LiFePO4 storage and 1,800 watts of output, enough to start and run a modern refrigerator for most of a day or a CPAP for several nights. It makes no noise, needs no fuel or oil, and recharges from a wall outlet in about an hour, from solar panels, or from a small gas inverter running outdoors. That last combination is the clever one: run the generator for an hour or two in the daytime, then let the battery carry the fridge and internet silently through the night. For outages longer than a day with no solar, it needs a fuel-burning partner. At the time of writing it sells for roughly $450 to $650.

sections.heading: What Counts as a Small Generator for Home Backup?
sections.body:
A small home generator is one that one or two adults can move without a truck ramp, producing roughly 1,600 to about 4,000 running watts. Most are enclosed inverter models with 120-volt outlets only and a fuel tank holding one to three and a half gallons. The suitcase-style units weigh under 40 pounds, and the biggest wheeled models reach about 100.

### Why are most outage loads small enough?

The class exists because the loads that matter in most outages are modest. Averaged across a day, a modern refrigerator uses around 100 to 150 watts. A gas furnace blower draws a few hundred watts, and LED lights plus internet gear add a couple of hundred more. The loads that wreck a list, such as central air conditioning, electric water heaters, electric ranges and dryers, and 240-volt well pumps, are the ones a small generator never tries to carry.

### What does a small generator do better than a big one?

The benefits stack up. Burning less fuel matters when gas stations are closed. Lower noise matters at night and next to close neighbors. A smaller unit also costs less, stores more easily and is far simpler to roll out and start in the dark, which is exactly when outages tend to arrive.

### Can a small generator power a whole house?

No, and that is the wrong test. The useful question is whether it can run the parts of the house you truly depend on during an outage, and for a large share of homes with gas heat it can. Homes on a well, homes with electric heat and homes in hot climates where air conditioning is a safety matter should start with the larger machines in our [full outage generator rankings](/best-home-generator-for-power-outages/). If gasoline is the fuel you plan around and you need more than a small unit offers, the [gas generator guide](/best-gas-generator/) covers the bigger gasoline portables.

sections.heading: What Will a Small Generator Actually Power?
sections.body:
A small generator will run a refrigerator, lights, internet and electronics, plus a gas furnace blower or a sump pump depending on its size, as long as the motors start one at a time. Every motor needs a brief surge to get going, which makes the starting rating as important as the running rating. A refrigerator compressor that runs on 150 to 200 watts can demand 1,000 to 2,000 watts for about a second at start-up. Letting the fridge, freezer and sump pump start in turn, rather than all together, is the main skill with a small unit.

| Generator size | Comfortably runs | Stretch loads | Will not run |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| About 1,700-1,850W running | Fridge plus lights, internet, TV, phones; or furnace blower plus lights | Microwave alone, with everything else off | Fridge and freezer and sump together; any 240V load |
| About 3,000W running | Fridge, freezer, lights, internet, sump pump | Window AC with fridge, if staggered | Central AC, well pump, electric water heater |
| About 3,700W running | Fridge, freezer, sump, furnace blower, lights, electronics | Small window AC on top of essentials | Central AC, 240V well pump, electric range |

### How do you find your appliances' real wattage?

Start with each appliance's data plate: running amps multiplied by 120 gives a fair estimate of running watts. Better still, put a plug-in watt meter on the refrigerator for a full day. It reports both the running draw and the daily average, and the average is the number that drives fuel planning. Older refrigerators and chest freezers can use two or three times as much as a new model, so measure rather than guess.

### Which appliances overload a small generator?

The quiet budget-wreckers are microwaves, coffee makers, toasters and hair dryers, each pulling 1,000 to 1,500 watts while it runs. On a 2,200-watt generator, use them one at a time with nothing else heavy running, and plan meals around that limit. For outage cooking, a propane camp stove used outdoors beats any electric appliance on a small generator.

Typical Small-Generator Loads

100-200W

Refrigerator, running

300-800W

Gas furnace blower

800-1,050W

Sump pump, running

1,000-1,500W

Microwave or coffee maker

sections.heading: Why Should a Small Home Generator Be an Inverter?
sections.body:
Because an inverter burns less fuel, runs quieter and makes cleaner power, and at the small end it no longer costs much more. A conventional generator holds its engine at a fixed speed so the alternator puts out 60 hertz directly. An inverter generator makes raw power at whatever engine speed the load calls for, converts it to DC and then electronically back into clean 60-hertz AC. Three practical results follow for home backup.

### Does an inverter really save fuel?

Yes. The engine slows down when demand is low, so an inverter carrying a refrigerator and a few lights burns a fraction of what it would at full throttle, which is how a one-gallon tank can last most of a night. A conventional open-frame unit of similar size burns fuel at nearly the same rate whether it is powering one lamp or its full rating.

### What else does an inverter do better?

The slower engine speed and the enclosed, muffled case make inverters far quieter at light load. The power is better too: inverter output has low total harmonic distortion, which is gentler on electronics, variable-speed furnace motors and the control boards inside modern appliances. Many furnace makers recommend clean generator power for exactly that reason.

### Is a conventional generator ever the better buy?

Price is the only real case, and at the small end that gap has largely closed. Inexpensive 2,000-watt inverters now cost about what a conventional 3,500-watt open frame does, and they make the better outage tool in almost every way except raw surge. Unless your goal is the cheapest possible watts for running power tools, choose an inverter. Our [inverter generator guide](/best-inverter-generator/) covers the wider category beyond home backup.

sections.heading: How Quiet Is a Small Generator, and Where Should You Put It?
sections.body:
A good small inverter is about as loud as normal conversation at 23 feet, but where you place it changes what the neighbors hear as much as the rating does. Noise figures are usually taken at about 7 meters, or roughly 23 feet, often at a quarter load. Honda rates the EU2200i at 48 to 57 dBA, which most people compare to conversation at that distance. Large open-frame portables commonly rate in the low to mid 70s dBA, and because the decibel scale is logarithmic, every 10-decibel step sounds about twice as loud.

### Where is the best place to run it?

The spot that keeps carbon monoxide out of your house, at least 20 feet away with the exhaust pointed away from doors, windows and vents, also has to respect the neighbors' windows. On a tight suburban lot that often means the open middle of the backyard rather than the side yard between two homes, where exhaust can drift into either one.

### Does the surface under it matter?

Yes. Hard surfaces bounce sound, so a generator on concrete beside a fence sounds louder next door than the same unit on grass in the open. Never build a closed box around a running generator to muffle it. Any enclosure has to be designed for running operation with enough airflow, or the engine overheats and exhaust collects around it.

### Are there rules about running a generator at night?

Some neighborhoods set quiet hours, and some HOAs restrict generator use or storage, so read yours before a storm arrives. In practice, neighbors tolerate a quiet inverter running a refrigerator far better than a big open-frame unit droning all night, especially if you shut it off for a few hours at a stretch once the fridge is cold.

sections.heading: Can You Parallel Two Small Generators for More Power?
sections.body:
Yes, if both units are parallel-capable and come from the same maker. Many small inverters link through a parallel kit, a short set of cables that combines two units' output. Two 2,200-watt units together give roughly 3,600 running and 4,400 starting watts, enough for a fridge and lights plus a sump pump or one window air conditioner, while each generator stays light enough to carry on its own.

### Can you mix brands in a parallel setup?

Generally not. Parallel operation works best with two identical units from one manufacturer; mixing brands is usually unsupported, and some makers allow pairing only within a specific model family. Read both manuals before buying a second unit for this purpose. Some kits add a 30-amp outlet, which makes connecting to a transfer switch inlet easier.

### What are the pros and cons of running two units?

The appeal is flexibility. A short outage needs only one unit for the fridge and lights; when the outage drags on or the sump pump is cycling hard, you start the second. Each unit is easier to store, carry and start than a single 4,000-watt machine, and if one fails you still have the other.

The costs are real. Two Hondas cost more than one large portable, the maintenance doubles, and there are twice as many small tanks to refill. Two generators also mean two exhausts, and both must follow the same placement rules. If you know from the start that you need 3,500 watts or more, a single iGen4500 is the simpler route.

### How should you set up a parallel kit?

Buy the kit along with the second generator and rehearse the connection once in daylight. Owners commonly report that the cables themselves are simple, but locating the right outlet panel cover and remembering which unit to start first goes much better on a calm afternoon than in the middle of a storm.

sections.heading: How Do You Connect a Small Generator to Your House Safely?
sections.body:
Run outdoor-rated extension cords straight to the appliances, or have an electrician install a transfer switch or interlock; never use a wall outlet. Cords are how most small generator owners do it, and that is safe and legal when it is done right: outdoor-rated, heavy-gauge cords, 12-gauge for long runs or heavier loads, with no damaged insulation. Do not feed them through a window or door that then has to stay open and let exhaust inside; a dedicated cord port through the wall solves that problem.

SAFETY RULE

Never plug a generator into a wall outlet.

Pushing power into a household receptacle with a double-ended male cord sends it back through your panel and out onto the utility lines. The pole transformer raises that voltage, and line workers can be electrocuted. It also bypasses the protection of your main breaker, and when grid power returns it can wreck the generator or start a fire. In most places it is illegal.

### How do you power a hardwired furnace or sump pump?

Hardwired loads such as a gas furnace blower, or a sump pump on its own circuit, need a transfer switch or a panel interlock with an outdoor inlet, installed by a licensed electrician under a permit. Small generators suit this well: a 20- or 30-amp 120-volt inlet and a handful of chosen circuits cover most small setups. Our [generator transfer switch guide](/best-generator-transfer-switch/) compares the hardware.

### Does a 120-volt generator work with a transfer switch?

It can, but it takes planning. A home panel has two 120-volt legs, and a 120-volt generator naturally feeds only one of them. Electricians solve that in different ways depending on the switch, the panel and local code, and it is never a job for homemade adapters. Give your electrician the generator model and the list of circuits you want powered, and let them design the connection.

### Should you add surge protection?

While the electrician is on site, ask about a [whole-house surge protector](/best-whole-house-surge-protector/). Electronics are most exposed to spikes at two moments: when utility power comes back after an outage, and when the house switches between sources.

sections.heading: How Much Fuel Does a Small Generator Use in an Outage?
sections.body:
Not much: a 2,000-watt class inverter at a quarter load commonly runs around 8 hours on about a gallon of gasoline. At half load, expect roughly half that time. The iGen4500's 3.4-gallon tank goes much further at light loads. Makers measure run times under ideal conditions, so plan on a little less than the listed figure.

### How much gas should you store for a three-day outage?

Running a small inverter mostly at light load around the clock for three days takes roughly 6 to 12 gallons of gasoline. Running it in blocks, a few hours on to chill the fridge and freezer and then off, cuts that considerably. A refrigerator left closed keeps food at safe temperatures for about four hours, and a full freezer holds out much longer.

### How should you store generator fuel?

Keep gasoline in approved containers, with stabilizer added when you fill them, in a detached shed or garage away from ignition sources and never inside the house. Rotate it into your car every few months. Stale fuel that varnishes the carburetor causes many small-engine starting failures, so run the generator under some load for 15 to 20 minutes every month, and follow the manual on storing it with stabilized fuel or with the carburetor run dry.

### Is refueling a small generator dangerous?

It can be. Refuel only with the engine off and cooled; small tanks need frequent top-ups, and gasoline spilled on a hot muffler is a genuine fire risk. For longer unattended runs, consider a dual fuel version that runs on propane cylinders, which several small inverter lines offer. Our [dual fuel inverter guide](/best-dual-fuel-inverter-generator/) covers those, and the [gas generator guide](/best-gas-generator/) goes deeper on gasoline logistics.

sections.heading: How Far From the House Should You Run a Small Generator?
sections.body:
At least 20 feet, with the exhaust aimed away from doors, windows and vents, and never inside any enclosed space. Being easy to carry makes a small generator easy to put in the wrong spot. A small engine still produces lethal carbon monoxide, far more than a car's exhaust, and the gas has no color or smell. Never run any generator in the house, a basement, a crawlspace, an attached garage, an enclosed porch or a shed, even with the doors open or a fan running.

### What does federal safety guidance say?

It puts the generator at least 20 feet from the house with the exhaust pointed away from doors, windows and vents. Make sure no window, attic vent or furnace intake sits downwind. Fit battery-powered or battery-backup CO alarms on every level of the home and outside sleeping areas, and test them before storm season.

### Does a CO shutoff make a generator safe to run closer?

No. Pick a generator with automatic CO shutoff, such as Honda's CO-MINDER, Champion's CO Shield or Generac's COsense, and look for a listing to ANSI/PGMA G300 or UL 2201 on the box. These systems stop the engine when CO builds up around it, guarding against the classic fatal mistake of running in a garage. They are never a reason to set the generator closer to the house.

### What are the signs of carbon monoxide poisoning?

Headache, dizziness, weakness, nausea and confusion in people, and lethargy in pets. If anyone feels this way or a CO alarm goes off, get everyone outside into fresh air at once and call 911.

sections.heading: How Do You Maintain a Small Generator So It Starts?
sections.body:
Give it about ten minutes a month: check the oil, start it and run it under a real load for 15 to 20 minutes. Small engines forgive a lot, but neglect shows up in one specific way, a varnished carburetor, and that monthly routine prevents it. Roll the generator out, check the oil on the dipstick or fill window, start it and plug in something real, such as a work light or a hair dryer on low. Running it with nothing plugged in does less for the system.

### How often should you change the oil?

After the short break-in period the manual lists, often the first few hours, then at the manual's hour interval or at least once a year. Small inverters hold well under a quart, so the job is quick and cheap. Keep a spare spark plug and air filter on the shelf; they cost little and save a store run during a storm.

### How should you store it between outages?

Somewhere dry and ventilated outside the living space, with stabilized fuel or a dry carburetor as the manual directs. A breathable cover keeps dust and mice out. Before hurricane or winter storm season, hold a full rehearsal: fuel it, start it, connect your actual extension cords or inlet, and run the refrigerator for an hour.

### Who else should know how to start it?

Everyone at home. Tape a laminated card to the generator with the starting steps and the order in which to add loads. The person who has to start it during an outage may not be the person who bought it, and clear instructions are worth more than any feature on the spec sheet.

sections.heading: When Is a Small Generator Too Small for Your Home?
sections.body:
When you rely on a 240-volt well pump, face multi-day outages or electric heat, need air conditioning for someone's health, or have essential loads above about 3,500 running watts. Any one of those points you toward a larger portable, a standby unit or a combined battery-and-generator plan.

### What if your home is on a well?

A private well with a 240-volt pump rules out most small generators, which are 120-volt only. You need a larger portable with a 240-volt outlet and a transfer switch, or a standby unit. Water is usually the first thing people miss in an outage, so treat this one seriously; our [well pump generator guide](/best-generator-for-well-pump/) covers sizing for that setup.

### What about long outages or electric heat?

If outages routinely run longer than three or four days, or your heat is electric, the fuel logistics of a week of running and the size of electric heat loads point to a larger portable on propane or a standby generator on natural gas. Our [Generac cost guide](/generac-generator-cost/) sets out what that step actually costs.

### Can a small generator run air conditioning?

One small window unit at most. If you live somewhere hot enough that air conditioning protects someone's health, and central air is non-negotiable, start with the larger machines and add a soft-start kit on the condenser.

### What if your load list keeps growing?

Once the must-run total climbs past about 3,500 running watts, one larger machine, or a battery station paired with a generator, beats pushing a small unit to its limit for days. A generator run near its maximum for long stretches wears faster, burns more fuel and gets louder.

mistakes.title: Starting every motor at the same moment
mistakes.body: A small generator can usually run the refrigerator, freezer and sump pump together, yet it may overload if all three start in the same instant. Switch on the largest motor first and let it settle before adding the next. If the unit trips, unplug everything, reset it and reconnect loads one by one.

mistakes.title: Expecting a small unit to run a well pump
mistakes.body: Most private wells use a 240-volt pump, while nearly every small inverter offers 120 volts only, and no adapter bridges that gap safely. A home on a well needs a larger portable with a 240-volt outlet and a transfer switch, or a standby generator, sized for the pump's starting surge.

mistakes.title: Parking it on the porch to keep it dry
mistakes.body: Covered porches, carports and breezeways beside the house trap exhaust, which then drifts in through doors and windows, and a small engine is no exception. Run the generator in the open at least 20 feet from the house, under a purpose-made generator tent or canopy, with battery CO alarms working indoors.

mistakes.title: Storing it with untreated gasoline
mistakes.body: Stale gasoline gums up a small carburetor fast, so a generator that ran perfectly last spring can refuse to start in the first winter storm. Add stabilizer every time you buy fuel, run the unit under load once a month, and store it the way the manual says: full of stabilized fuel or with the carburetor run dry.

mistakes.title: Running power through thin indoor cords
mistakes.body: Light-duty indoor cords overheat under a refrigerator or space heater and drop voltage, which compressors dislike. Use outdoor-rated cords of adequate gauge, 12-gauge for most generator runs, kept as short as practical and fully uncoiled. Never pinch them in a door or hide them under rugs, and check them for damage before each outage.

faqs.q: Can a 2,000-watt generator run a refrigerator?
faqs.a: Yes. A modern refrigerator draws roughly 100 to 200 watts while running and needs about 1,000 to 2,000 watts for an instant to start its compressor, which a 2,000-watt class inverter can supply. Lights, the internet and phone charging usually fit alongside it. Starting a freezer or microwave at the same moment is too much, so bring those loads on one at a time.

faqs.q: How many watts does a small house need in an outage?
faqs.a: In a home with gas heat, the essentials of a refrigerator, freezer, furnace blower, lights and internet usually fit within roughly 2,500 to 4,000 running watts. A sump pump moves you toward the top of that range. A 240-volt well pump, central air or electric heat calls for a larger generator. Read the appliance labels to get your real numbers.

faqs.q: Are small inverter generators safe for computers and TVs?
faqs.a: Yes. Inverter output is clean, with low harmonic distortion, which suits laptops, TVs, routers and the control boards in modern furnaces. Conventional open-frame generators can put out rougher power. A good surge protector is still worth using with an inverter, and it is a sensible habit to switch sensitive electronics off before you start or stop the generator.

faqs.q: How quiet are small generators really?
faqs.a: Quiet 2,000-watt class inverters are commonly rated from the low to the high 50s dBA at about 23 feet and light load, close to the level of normal conversation. Large open-frame portables often rate in the 70s. What the neighbors actually hear depends on load, surface, distance and nearby walls, so set the unit on grass in the open, not between houses.

faqs.q: Is it worth paralleling two small generators?
faqs.a: It can be. Two identical parallel-capable inverters deliver roughly twice the output, each unit stays easy to carry, and in a light outage you can run only one. The pair costs more than one larger generator and doubles the maintenance. If every outage will need more than 3,500 watts, one larger inverter is the simpler setup.

faqs.q: Can I connect a small generator to my electrical panel?
faqs.a: Only through a transfer switch, or a listed panel interlock with an outdoor inlet, installed by a licensed electrician under a permit. Never plug the generator into a wall outlet: that backfeeds the grid and puts line workers at risk. Many small 120-volt generators need the electrician to plan how they feed the panel, so give them your model before the install.

faqs.q: Small gas generator or battery station: which comes first?
faqs.a: Start with a battery station if your outages are short, you live in an apartment or someone in the home uses a CPAP, because it runs silently indoors. If outages stretch past a day, a small gas inverter supplies far more total energy for the money. Many households own both and run the generator outdoors in short bursts to recharge the battery.

bottomLine:
The Honda EU2200i is the small generator to own for most homes with gas heat and modest outage needs, and the Champion 2500-watt ultralight is the value pick. When a sump pump, freezer and furnace all need power together, move up to the Westinghouse iGen4500 or the Generac GP3500iO.

Run it outdoors at least 20 feet from the house with the exhaust aimed away, feed the house through cords or a proper transfer switch and never a wall outlet, and give it a monthly run on stabilized fuel. Handled that way, a small generator will quietly see you through most outages.
